intro: You are at Karain Cave, in Antalya province, and the story here begins about 500,000 years ago. This great karst cave is one of the oldest known human dwellings in Anatolia, used without a break from the Palaeolithic to the classical age.
history: The cave lies at the foot of Mount Katran, and for roughly half a million years it was in use without a break. Its layers have yielded Neanderthal as well as Homo sapiens remains, hearths, and tools of stone and bone. In the classical period its mouth became a sanctuary, with votive niches and inscriptions cut into the rock. Pause and imagine the generations who sheltered here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the main chambers and the votive niches and inscriptions, then the excavation sections and the Karain Museum.
facts: Did you know? Karain was the first Palaeolithic cave excavated in Türkiye, and the first evidence of Neanderthals in Anatolia came out of it. Its deposits are eleven metres deep and hold an unbroken sequence of half a million years of occupation; there is nothing else like it in Türkiye. The first Neanderthal remains found in Anatolia came from here, and traces of Homo sapiens occur in the same layers.
outro: This brings our journey through Karain Cave to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. People have sheltered here for half a million years; let the cave keep its story for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
